course_title: Multiliteracies and Numeracy Across Learning Areas

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate comprehensive and well-founded knowledge of the current nature of literacy and numeracy in the twenty first century
Critically review contemporary international and national empirical research on literacy and numeracy learning across curricula
Apply contemporary international and national empirical research on literacy and numeracy learning to teaching and learning design across learning areas
Design an action research project that investigates an aspect of multiliteracies and/or numeracy teaching and learning as a means of professional development and pedagogical improvement.

assessments.assessment_title: Action Research Proposal: Inquiry question, Literature review and Plan
assessments.task_description:
Action Research Project Overview:

Reflecting on the benefits of action research for professional learning is a useful way of improving your understanding of your role as a practitioner and as an educational researcher. Across EDUC7113 the contemporary landscape of multiliteracies and numeracy will be mapped and explored. With this understanding you will identify a key multiliteracy or numeracy challenge or issue that you will explore across the semester. This will be the focus of Assessment 1, 2 and 3. 

Assessment Task 1 has 3 parts, and will be up to 2000 words total (excluding references):

 Part 1 – Inquiry Question (approx. 250 words)

Action research in education is a cyclical, reflective research practice that many experienced teachers engage in. It often involves choosing a topic, framing the research problem statement and formulating specific research question/s (guided by the literature review) (Efron & David, 2020).

  • If you are currently a practising teacher, it is important for the action research to be small scale and manageable.
  • If you are not currently practicing as a teacher you may look at inquiring into something that you are interested in, perplexed by or want to change, by analysing resources and/or talking to educators (e.g. policies, curricula, research, educational programs, interviewing curriculum leaders and/or teachers) to inform your future practice.


In Part 1 you are to define your inquiry focus by briefly describing the educational context and the challenge or issue you wish to address as a problem statement. You will construct key research question/s to address the issue in Part 3. You will be required to share your research topic, problem statement and potential research question/s (on the Blackboard Discussion and during class in week 2 or 3) to receive feedback from the Lecturer and your peers.

 Part 2 – Literature Review (approx.1250 words)

  • Conduct a literature review of the challenge or issue you identified in Part 1. Gather information from peer-reviewed academic literature, policies, reports, etc. to situate your problem within education context/s
  • Consolidate all this information into a literature review demonstrating synthesis, critical analysis, evaluation and identification of any gaps in research.
  • Discuss how this literature shapes your understanding of the topic and how it helps you justify your inquiry.

 

Part 3 – Project plan (approx. 500 words)

  • Identify your key research question/s you are going to investigate (and explain how it/they are informed by your literature review)
  • Design and describe the action research you will undertake (over the coming weeks) to understand the phenomena of your inquiry, informed by your review of the issue.
  • Explain how each action connects to your inquiry focus and the literature.
  • List what data you will gather (e.g., student responses, observations, personal reflections of practice).
  • Provide an estimated timeframe for each action.


References

  • Efron, E.E, & Ravid, R. (2020). Action Research in Education : A Practical Guide, Guilford Publications https://ebookcentral.proquest.com/lib/uql/detail.action?docID=5928892

assessments.assessment_title: Action Research Implementation report: Outcomes and Response
assessments.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Presentation, Portfolio, Poster
assessments.task_description:
For this task, you will communicate the results or outcomes of your action research plan (outlined in Task 1) in a format you feel best communicates the findings. This choice is open to oral, written, presentation. audio-visual product, or a combination of the above. You may submit up to 2000 words, a presentation of up to 12 mins, poster, or a multimodal product of an equivalent length.  

Your submission in any of the formats, should cover:

  • Introduction: Briefly describe the research context and your problem statement (from Task 1).
  • Methodology/Action research implementation: Describe the actions you undertook (according to your plan from Task 1)
  • Data and Analysis: Describe the data you collected, how you analysed it, and the findings
  • Discussion: Describe your findings in relation to your initial research question/s and the wider research literature
  • Conclusion and implications: Discuss what you have learned through your action research, what implications your project has raised and how it will influence your future practice

assessments.task_description:
Students are required to reflect on their action research project in a one-one-one online meeting with the lecturer. They will briefly describe their project and results. They will be required to answer (unseen) reflective questions from the lecturer about their implementation of their project, as well as situate their project in relation to the current landscape of multiliteracies and/or numeracy research.

Reflections will be based on discussion of content submitted in Assessment Tasks 1 and 2.

Students are able to consult one A4 page of printed notes/images during the discussion.
